implementation_notes: circe's JsonObject exposes insertion-ordered toIterable plus remove/mapValues, so a projection is a filter over the encoded resource and a rebuild (or json.mapObject(...)); a Tapir/http4s endpoint decodes the fields query parameter with a QueryParamDecoder and passes the set down. The case class stays the single description of the resource, and the projection is a pure function - which is why this is the default Scala realization.
pitfalls: JsonObject.toMap drops insertion order (documented), so use toIterable - otherwise the reply key order wobbles between runs.
Rebuilding a JsonObject silently keeps the last duplicate key, which hides upstream encoder bugs that would otherwise be visible.
Projection happens after the full case class was encoded: for large resources write a per-view Encoder instead, and remember nested JsonObject/JsonArray need the same treatment recursively.

variants.name: Caliban GraphQL selection sets
variants.idiom_name: case-class-derived GraphQL schema; only selected fields are resolved
variants.implementation_notes: Caliban derives the schema from case classes and resolves only the fields the client selected, so the selection set *is* the mask and no filters are applied after the fact. Fields that must be hidden or that are expensive get explicit directives/exclusions, and resolvers can inspect the selection for batching. Choose this when the whole boundary is GraphQL; a REST endpoint with a fields parameter stays with the circe variant.
variants.code_sketch:
case class User(id: UserId, email: String, createdAt: Instant)
case class Queries(user: UserId => ZIO[Any, Throwable, Option[User]])

val api = graphQL(RootResolver(Queries(id => repo.find(id))))
// client: { user(id: "42") { id email } }  - createdAt is never resolved
pitfalls: Derived schemas expose everything by default: fields with permission rules need explicit exclusions/directives, or a client simply names what it should not see.
Effectful resolvers still run per selected field - batching (ZQuery/DataLoader) is required to avoid N+1 queries when several objects are projected at once.
Schema derivation is compile-time: making a field conditionally visible requires code, not a mask value, so 'views' become schema variants.
